literal: Distress to those who possess grace there is not; the wind-blowing, abundant and great world is the witness.
translation: There is no suffering for those who possess compassion; the vast, fertile world blown by the wind is the witness to this truth.
modern: அருள் உடையவர்களுக்குத் துன்பம் இல்லை; காற்று வீசுகின்ற வளம் பொருந்திய பெரிய உலகமே இதற்குச் சாட்சியாகும்.
explanation: This couplet declares that those who live with compassion and grace will never experience distress. To prove this, the poet summons the entire vast, fertile earth sustained by the blowing wind as a witness. The phrase 'வளிவழங்கும் மல்லன்மா ஞாலம்' highlights the grandeur of the physical world, emphasizing that the natural order itself stands testimony to the peace and safety enjoyed by compassionate souls. By showing mercy to all living beings, one remains free from misery.
